leads.title: French Penal Code, Article 225-1 as amended 18 November 2016
leads.documents: Criminal ban on discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation and gender identity; core legal protection applicable in Réunion as overseas department.
leads.detail: Cited as article 225-1 Code pénal; 1985 law for sexual orientation, July 2012 added 'sexual identity', 18 November 2016 law replaced with 'gender identity'

leads.title: French Labour Code, Chapter 2 - Code du travail
leads.documents: Prohibits exclusion from recruitment, sanction or dismissal on account of sexual orientation and gender identity; employment rights machinery.
leads.detail: Quoted text: 'No person may be excluded from a recruitment process...' listing origin, gender, morals, sexual orientation, gender identity, etc.

leads.title: Law of 31 December 2004 and Law on the Freedom of the Press of 29 July 1881, Title 3, Articles 20 and 21
leads.documents: Hate-crime/speech machinery; increased penalties when assault/murder motivated by sexual orientation; created Haute autorité de lutte contre les discriminations et pour l'égalité.
leads.detail: National Assembly approved 31 December 2004 amendment; max penalty cited as €45,000 fine and/or 12 months imprisonment; Christian Vanneste conviction Jan 2006 cancelled by Court of Cassation

leads.title: European Court of Human Rights - B. vs France (1992)
leads.documents: Court ruling that ended French ban on legal gender change and required recognition; foundation for transgender legal status in France including Réunion.
leads.detail: Cited as 1992 case B. vs France at the European Court of Human Rights changing prior ban

leads.title: Law of 18 November 2016 on legal gender change, effective 1 January 2017
leads.documents: Allows transgender people to change gender marker without surgery/sterilization via court order; first-name change via registry office.
leads.detail: Senate 6 Nov 2015, National Assembly 24 May 2016 and 12 July 2016 and 12 Oct, Senate 28 Sept, Constitutional Council ruled constitutional 17 Nov, signed 18 Nov 2016, published Journal Officiel next day, took effect 1 Jan 2017

leads.title: Law of 17-18 May 2013 legalising same-sex marriage and adoption
leads.documents: Establishes same-sex marriage and joint adoption legality nationwide including all overseas departments and territories such as Réunion.
leads.detail: National Assembly 329-229 on 12 Feb 2013 and 23 April, Senate 179-157 on 9 April and 12 April, Constitutional Council ruled constitutional 17 May 2013, signed by President Francois Hollande 18 May 2013, published Journal Officiel next day, first ceremony 29 May Montpellier

leads.title: 2013 National Assembly vote breakdown for overseas deputies including Réunion
leads.documents: Documents direct legislative applicability and political context in Réunion: 3 Réunion deputies voted for same-sex marriage, 2 voted against, 1 not present.
leads.detail: Of 27 overseas deputies: 11 for (2 Mayotte, 3 Réunion, 1 French Guiana, 1 Guadeloupe, 1 Martinique, 2 New Caledonia, 1 Saint Pierre and Miquelon), 11 against, 1 abstained, 3 absent

leads.title: ILGA-Europe Report published 2022 on gender-affirming healthcare in France
leads.documents: Institutional human-rights report documenting lack of self-determination, extended waiting times, inequitable access by location; recommends informed consent model.
leads.detail: Cited as 2022 ILGA-Europe report finding significant issues with provision of gender affirming healthcare in France

leads.title: DILCRAH - French Interministerial Delegation for the Fight Against Racism, Anti-Semitism, and Anti-LGBT Hatred
leads.documents: Government rights machinery responsible for anti-LGBT hatred policy; 2022 controversy over scientific committee president membership in The Little Mermaid Observatory.
leads.detail: Cited as DILCRAH with scientific committee; one member resigned, president publicly stepped away from The Observatory in 2022

leads.title: Police figures reported 16 May 2020 before International Day Against Homophobia, Transphobia and Biphobia
leads.documents: Documented enforcement/incident data: homophobic and transphobic attacks/insults rose 36% in 2019 with ~1,870 victims vs ~1,380 in 2018.
leads.detail: Report released 16 May 2020 right before IDAHOTB; police identified around 1,870 victims of transphobic and homophobic attacks
